notes: A distributed-ops bring-up emulator. The operator edits one XML site config (address/port/complementary role bindings), then writes a boot pipeline that starts a long-lived dependent gateway, waits for its readiness signal, launches and keeps alive three JVM daemon roles that bind their role ports (port, port+1, port+2), and verifies reachability with a compatible client. Alongside: a strict-format SLURM-style monitor generator (one header, ISO-8601 UTC second timestamp, 3-decimal load fraction), a named SlurmLauncher config that must resolve by name without changing job submission fields, a runner settings file recording a resolvable python3 interpreter path, and env exports persisted in the shell rc so a fresh shell sees them. Hits every competency floor at least; the max floor among the seven competencies is medium, so the task is medium (sum 13). Hidden-case generalization: the grader rotates the SLURM stand-in node state across four genuinely different scenarios and re-runs monitor_gen.sh, requiring the counts and fraction (including 0.000 and 1.000 edges) to be recomputed from the live state. Debugging_ambiguity lives in the exact monitor format (single header, strict timestamp, 3-decimal fraction) and in the port-offset + readiness-ordering semantics that crash-loop a role if the config mds.address/rpc.port or a role binding is wrong.
